title: use justfile for multi-arch build orchestration
description:
## Decision

Use justfile (just command runner) to provide standardized recipes for building, testing, and pushing multi-architecture images.

## Rationale

- Simple, readable task definitions without Makefile complexity.
- Variable-based design (name, namespace, dockerfile, platforms) makes recipes reusable across services with minimal changes.
- Recipes are self-documenting via just --list.
- Supports importing shared recipe files (just import) for future cross-repo reuse.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Makefile**: Verbose syntax, whitespace-sensitive, less readable.
- **Shell scripts**: No dependency/ordering support, harder to discover available tasks.
- **Task (taskfile.dev)**: YAML-based, more overhead for simple recipes.

## Affects

- All local build and push workflows; CI can call just recipes for consistency

title: use docker buildx over Apple container tool for multi-arch builds
description:
## Decision

Use docker buildx exclusively for multi-architecture image builds on all platforms.

## Rationale

Apple's container tool has serious DNS resolution failures during builds — packages cannot be fetched from Alpine APK or Go module proxy. docker buildx works reliably on both macOS and Linux.

## Alternatives Considered

- **apple/container (OS-conditional routing)**: Implemented first but abandoned due to DNS failures blocking apk add and go mod download inside the build.
- **Separate CI-only builds**: Rejected — developers need to build locally to test.

## Affects

- justfile recipes: build-multiarch, build-amd64, build-arm64, push-ghcr

title: apply UPX compression on amd64 only, skip on arm64
description:
## Decision

UPX binary compression is applied conditionally: only when TARGETARCH=amd64.

## Rationale

UPX is not reliable on arm64 — it causes build failures and corrupted binaries in Alpine + QEMU emulation scenarios. amd64 builds benefit from ~60-70% size reduction with no such issues.

## Alternatives Considered

- **UPX on all architectures**: Breaks arm64 builds.
- **No UPX at all**: Larger amd64 image for no benefit.
- **upx --best on arm64 only**: Unreliable; dropped.

## Affects

- Dockerfile.multiarch builder stage RUN steps

title: Multi-Architecture Docker Build Support
description: Implement multi-architecture Docker image builds using docker buildx, following the architectural decisions from modware-stock. This epic covers justfile orchestration, Dockerfile modifications for Alpine + distroless, conditional UPX compression, and cross-compilation support.

title: Create justfile with multi-arch build orchestration
description:
Create justfile with recipes for building, testing, and pushing multi-architecture Docker images. Include variables for image name, namespace, platforms (linux/amd64,linux/arm64), and dockerfile path.

**Recipes to implement:**
- build-multiarch: Build for all platforms using docker buildx
- build-amd64: Build amd64 only for quick local testing
- build-arm64: Build arm64 only for quick local testing  
- push-ghcr: Tag and push to GitHub Container Registry
- test: Run Go tests before building

**Decision Reference:** modware-annotation-5z6 (justfile rationale)
**Decision Reference:** modware-annotation-bmn (docker buildx requirement)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- justfile exists in repo root
- just --list shows all recipes with descriptions
- Variables defined at top for easy customization
- Buildx commands use --platform flag correctly
close_reason: Justfile created with all required recipes (test, build-multiarch, build-amd64, build-arm64, push-ghcr). Variables configured for easy customization. Docker buildx commands use --platform flags correctly. Code review approved - ready for production.

title: Update Dockerfile for multi-architecture support
description:
Modify build/package/Dockerfile to support multi-architecture builds with cross-compilation.

**Changes required:**
1. Switch FROM golang:1.24-bullseye → golang:1.24-alpine
2. Add ARG BUILDPLATFORM, TARGETPLATFORM, TARGETOS, TARGETARCH
3. Use --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM for builder stage
4. Set GOOS=$TARGETOS and GOARCH=$TARGETARCH (remove hardcoded amd64)
5. Add conditional UPX compression (only for amd64):
   ```dockerfile
   RUN if [ "$TARGETARCH" = "amd64" ]; then upx -q -9 /bin/app; fi
   ```
6. Keep gcr.io/distroless/static runtime (already correct)

**Decision References:**
- modware-annotation-f5l (BUILDPLATFORM/TARGETPLATFORM cross-compilation)
- modware-annotation-yqs (Alpine + distroless)
- modware-annotation-d1h (conditional UPX)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Dockerfile builds successfully for both amd64 and arm64
- CGO_ENABLED=0 set for static binary
- UPX only runs on amd64 builds
- No hardcoded architecture values
notes:
IMPORTANT: Create a new separate Dockerfile (e.g., Dockerfile.multiarch or build/package/Dockerfile.multiarch) instead of modifying the existing single-arch Dockerfile. This preserves the original for reference and allows gradual migration.

The new Dockerfile should be referenced in the justfile variable (update justfile to point to the new multi-arch Dockerfile).
close_reason: Dockerfile.multiarch created with correct ARG scoping, Alpine builder, distroless runtime, conditional UPX on amd64 only, and cross-compilation support. Justfile updated. Both spec and code quality reviews approved.

title: Configure docker buildx for multi-platform builds
description:
Set up docker buildx builder instance for multi-platform image builds.

**Setup steps:**
1. Create/configure buildx builder with multi-platform support:
   ```bash
   docker buildx create --name multiarch --use
   docker buildx inspect --bootstrap
   ```

2. Verify platforms available:
   ```bash
   docker buildx inspect | grep Platforms
   # Should include: linux/amd64, linux/arm64
   ```

3. Document in README or CONTRIBUTING.md:
   - One-time setup required
   - How to verify buildx is configured
   - How to switch between builders if needed

**Decision Reference:** modware-annotation-bmn (docker buildx requirement)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Buildx builder created and active
- Both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 platforms available
- Documentation added for developer setup
- justfile recipes use the configured builder

title: Test and validate multi-arch builds
description:
Verify multi-architecture build system works correctly on local machine.

**Test scenarios:**
1. Build amd64 image locally:
   ```bash
   just build-amd64
   docker images | grep modware-annotation
   ```

2. Build arm64 image locally:
   ```bash
   just build-arm64
   docker images | grep modware-annotation
   ```

3. Build multi-arch (both platforms):
   ```bash
   just build-multiarch
   ```

4. Verify image sizes and UPX compression:
   - amd64 should be smaller (UPX compressed)
   - arm64 should be larger (no UPX)
   - Both should use distroless/static base

5. Test image functionality:
   ```bash
   docker run --rm <image-name:tag> --help
   # Should show application help without errors
   ```

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All three build recipes work without errors
- Images are created for both platforms
- amd64 image shows ~60-70% size reduction from UPX
- arm64 image builds without UPX errors
- Both images run successfully and show expected output
- Document any issues or quirks discovered during testing

title: Replace ADD with COPY and pin distroless base image in Dockerfiles
description:
Follow-up from code quality review of ebl.2. Address Dockerfile best practices in both Dockerfiles.

**Issues to fix:**
1. Replace ADD with COPY in both Dockerfiles (hadolint DL3020)
   - build/package/Dockerfile: lines with ADD cmd, ADD internal
   - build/package/Dockerfile.multiarch: lines with ADD cmd, ADD internal

2. Pin distroless base image to specific tag (hadolint DL3006)
   - build/package/Dockerfile: gcr.io/distroless/static → gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot
   - build/package/Dockerfile.multiarch: same

3. Pin UPX version in Alpine (hadolint DL3018)
   - apk add --no-cache upx → apk add --no-cache upx=<version>

title: cross-compile using BUILDPLATFORM/TARGETPLATFORM Docker args
description:
## Decision

Builder stage uses --platform=\$BUILDPLATFORM (native host) and cross-compiles via GOOS/GOARCH targeting \$TARGETOS/\$TARGETARCH.

## Rationale

Building on the native host platform avoids slow QEMU emulation. Go cross-compilation is first-class and does not require emulation. amd64 builds on Apple Silicon are 5-10x faster this way.

## Alternatives Considered

- **QEMU emulation (--platform=\$TARGETPLATFORM for builder)**: Slow, especially for amd64 on arm64 host.
- **Separate native CI runners per arch**: More complex pipeline, not needed given Go's cross-compilation.

## Affects

- Dockerfile.multiarch FROM builder stage
- go build RUN step (CGO_ENABLED=0 required)

title: use Alpine builder and distroless/static runtime in Dockerfile
description:
## Decision

Two-stage Dockerfile: golang:1.24-alpine as builder, gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12 as runtime.

## Rationale

- Alpine gives apk tooling (upx, etc.) during build with a small footprint.
- distroless/static has no shell, no package manager, minimal attack surface — appropriate for a static Go binary.
- The combination produces a minimal, secure runtime image.

## Alternatives Considered

- **scratch**: No CA certificates or timezone data; painful for services making HTTPS calls.
- **Alpine runtime**: Larger image, shell present (unnecessary attack surface).
- **debian-slim runtime**: Larger, not needed for CGO_ENABLED=0 binary.

## Affects

- Dockerfile.multiarch both stages
